baseline.authority: docs/design/UI2_0_C2_JOB_EXECUTION_CONTRACT.md (FROZEN) is not the authority here; this movement is authorised by the Product Owner directly and constrained by AGENTS.md alone. The design reference is the committed identity study named below, and the Product Owner has rejected two prior attempts at it.
baseline.environment: Repository work only. No cluster, no host, no device.
baseline.observed: Two attempts have failed. Movement NXS-LOCAL-0182 was rejected on sight. The Product Owner assistant then drew SVG candidates by hand and the Product Owner rejected those too, in their words: not the slightest resemblance.
baseline.what_exists:
The reference is committed at docs/design/ui2_mockups/logo-identity-explorations.png -- a six-panel concept sheet. Option D, bottom-left, is the chosen direction.

What option D actually is, read off the sheet:
  - The word reads as ONE word: n-e-X-u-s, letters tightly kerned and touching,
    not three tokens with gaps.
  - The X is a true X: two diagonal strokes that CROSS. The stroke running one
    way is teal, the stroke running the other is blue, and the blue sits over
    the teal at the crossing.
  - The X is oversized against the lowercase letters: its arms rise above the
    x-height and drop below the baseline, and it visually locks into the e and
    the u rather than floating between them.
  - A heavy geometric sans, very dark navy.
  - Beneath, in wide-tracked capitals: A CLEARER TOMORROW.
  - An app mark: a dark navy rounded square carrying the two-tone X alone.

What the application ships today, and why it was rejected
(ui2/frontend/src/brand/NexusWordmark.tsx, ui2/frontend/src/brand/NexusMark.tsx):
the word renders as `ne X us` with visible gaps, the X is an ordinary letter at
ordinary size in one flat colour, nothing crosses or overlaps, and the tagline
is absent.

What the assistants hand-drawn attempt got wrong, so it is not repeated: the two
strokes were parallelograms placed side by side instead of crossing, which read
as a Y rather than an X, and ne and us sat far apart from the mark.

The products palette, for the navy: ui2/frontend/src/theme/m3Theme.ts.

recommended_reasoning.reason: Visual design judgement against a reference that two lighter attempts failed to match. The work is interpretation, not implementation.

requirements: The X must cross. Two strokes that meet without crossing are the failure of the last attempt and are the single thing to get right.
The word must read as one word. If the kerning makes it look like separate tokens, it is wrong.
Every asset must render identically without any font installed, which is why the letters are paths.
State in the pull request how each value was obtained -- sampled, measured, or chosen -- and never present a guess as a measurement.
risks: The reference is a raster concept sheet, so exact vector geometry has to be reconstructed by eye and measurement. Say which parts were measured and which were judged.
Two attempts have already been rejected for looking nothing like the reference. Producing something merely competent but different is the failure mode here, not producing something ugly.

in: Sample the actual colours from the reference PNG rather than estimating them, and state the sampled values in the pull request.
Produce the wordmark as SVG with the letterforms as PATHS, not as a text element bound to a font that will not exist on every machine.
Produce at minimum: wordmark with tagline, wordmark without tagline, the app mark alone, and a light-on-dark variant of each.
Produce a static preview page showing every variant at large, medium and small sizes, including the app mark at 32 pixels, so the Product Owner can judge before anything is wired in.
Commit the assets under a clearly named directory and say in the pull request which file is which.
out: Editing NexusWordmark.tsx, NexusMark.tsx or any application screen. The Product Owner chooses first; wiring is a later movement.
Inventing a different concept. Options A, B, C, E and F exist on the sheet and were not chosen; this movement draws D.
Adding a font dependency or a web font to the application.
